parties: <cite index="2-1">Purvah Green Power Private Limited (acquirer, subsidiary of CESC Limited) and ReNew Solar Power Private Limited (seller)</cite>
headline: <cite index="1-1">Purvah Green Power acquires six operational renewable energy SPVs (1.4GW, 1,411.48 MWDC) from ReNew Solar Power in ₹4,859 cr deal</cite>
sum: <cite index="3-2">CESC subsidiary Purvah Green Power acquires six ReNew SPVs holding 1,411.48 MWp of operational renewable capacity across Rajasthan and Karnataka at ₹4,859 cr enterprise value</cite>. <cite index="1-7">Post-completion, Purvah's contracted renewable capacity increases to 4.8GW (1.8GW operational, 3GW under construction)</cite>.
implication: <cite index="6-6">Deal marks shift from greenfield pipeline to operating assets anchored by contracted cash flows-a portfolio composition inflection for India's emerging renewable platforms</cite>; no regulatory approval required, accelerating completion timeline.
detail: <cite index="24-1,24-3">Purvah acquires 100% share capital of ReNew Hans Urja (810MW), ReNew Solar Photovoltaic (506.25MW), ReNew Wind Energy (Karnataka 3, MP Four, Karnataka 4) and ReNew Agni Power via SPA signed 10 Aug 2026</cite>. <cite index="4-4,4-10,4-11">Over 90% of capacity contracted with SECI under 25-year PPAs; remainder with Karnataka DISCOMs (BESCOM/HESCOM), all at 25-year tenor</cite>. <cite index="1-6">Deal valued at INR 48.59 billion (US$509 million), excluding contingent earn-out of INR 2.3 billion linked to change-in-law claims</cite>. <cite index="3-6">Completion expected before 31 October 2026</cite>.

framework.note: M&A structure via SPA; subsidiary acquisition and corporate reorganization.
Generation licensing exemption for grid-connected assets; PPA framework and RPO mandates; no licence required for SPV ownership transfer.
M&A control clearance; asset transfer between private entities in renewable energy does not trigger substantive scrutiny given competitive structure.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30 & Schedule III
framework.note: Stock exchange filings for related-party/material acquisition announcements by CESC (acquirer parent).

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Sections 47–48, 49, Schedule VI
framework.note: SPV share sale treatment; transfer pricing compliance; no Tax Ruling sought (standard arm's length transaction).
ReNew is Nasdaq-listed; contingent earn-out creates forex repatriation headroom; FDI route not triggered (acquisition is domestic SPV transfer).

framework.ref: State Electricity Regulatory Commission Orders (Rajasthan, Karnataka)
framework.note: PPA transfer mechanics and change-in-law triggers; regulatory approval for PPA novation NOT required (seller-buyer substitution is routine).
Tariff determination and renewable energy certificate (REC) framework for acquired projects (SECI contracts exempt from REC fungibility).

framework.ref: Ministry of Power/MNRE Guidelines (Competitive Bidding, Change-in-Law)
framework.note: Portfolio's 25-year SECI contracts include change-in-law pass-through; earn-out payable on verified claims realization.

structure.consideration: <cite index="1-6">INR 48.59 billion enterprise value (US$509 million), excluding contingent earn-out of INR 2.3 billion for change-in-law realizations</cite>; <cite index="44-3">ReNew projected to receive ~INR 18.1 billion (US$190 million) cash at close, subject to working capital and debt adjustments</cite>.
conditions: <cite index="11-6">No governmental or regulatory approval required</cite>
<cite index="44-2">Definitive SPA signed 10 August 2026 among PGPPL, ReNew Solar Power PL and six project SPVs</cite>
<cite index="27-5">No government or regulatory approval is required</cite>
approvals: <cite index="34-1">Post-completion, target companies become step-down subsidiaries of CESC Limited</cite>
Internal CESC board / parent funding approval (standard for subsidiary-level acquisition)
structure.novel: <cite index="5-4,5-5">Among largest acquisitions of operating solar assets in India; shifts acquirer portfolio from greenfield development to immediate cash-generating operational assets</cite>. Contingent earn-out tied to regulatory change-in-law claims (2.3B INR) is material monetization mechanism for seller.

triggers.note: PPA novation from ReNew to Purvah; no licence required (generators unlicensed) but DISCOM/SECI may require counterparty credit assessment.

triggers.law: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
triggers.note: CESC (parent) must disclose material acquisition to NSE/BSE within 30 minutes of signing; ReNew (Nasdaq-listed) must file Form 6-K.
CESC shareholder approval for loans/guarantees to Purvah GrP may be required if acquisition funded via intra-group advance.

triggers.law: Income Tax Act, 1961, Sections 18(1)(h), 47, Schedule VI
triggers.note: Potential tax audit on acquisition pricing; change-in-law earn-out classification (contingent liability accounting).
